issues.legal_issue: In a rent-default eviction suit requiring a tenant to make a curative payment at the first hearing, the first hearing occurs after issues are framed and the suit is posted for trial.
material_facts: The suit sought eviction for arrears of rent under a provision allowing the tenant to avoid eviction by paying the required amounts at the first hearing.
The issues in the suit were framed after the tenant had tendered and deposited the money.
issues.conclusion: The first hearing for the purpose of the statutory payment requirement is the stage after issues have been framed, when the suit is posted for trial; it cannot occur earlier than the preliminary examination of the parties and settlement of issues.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20(4) of the U.P. Urban Building (Regulation of Letting, Rent & Eviction) Act, 1972 ties the tenant’s curative payment to the first hearing. The Court adopted the Allahabad High Court’s interpretation and relied on Order X Rule 1, Order XIV Rule 1(5), and Order XV Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, which indicate that the first hearing cannot precede preliminary examination and settlement of issues.

predicates.rent_default_eviction_suit: The proceeding seeks eviction on the ground of a tenant’s default in paying rent.
predicates.cure_payment_due_at_first_hearing: The governing rule permits the tenant to avoid eviction by making the required payment at the first hearing.

issues.definition: When a rent-default eviction suit makes a curative payment due at the first hearing, that hearing occurs after issues are framed and the suit is posted for trial.

issues.legal_issue: A payment tendered to the court and processed through a challan is treated as deposited on the date of tender or challan presentation when the treasury deposit follows afterward.
material_facts: The tenant tendered the required money to the court before the relevant hearing and a challan was processed.
The money was deposited in the treasury afterward, but before the issues were framed and the suit was posted for trial.
issues.conclusion: The treasury deposit related back to the date on which the money was tendered or the challan was presented, so the tenant’s payment was within time.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 20(4) of the U.P. Urban Building (Regulation of Letting, Rent & Eviction) Act, 1972, payment had to be made by the first hearing. The Court accepted the approach in Bankey Bahari v. Gopal Dass and Daya Ram v. Virender Kumar Goel: where money is tendered before the court, a challan is passed and the money is then deposited in the treasury using that challan, the deposit relates back to the tender or challan-presentation date.

predicates.rent_default_eviction_suit: The proceeding seeks eviction on the ground of a tenant’s default in paying rent.
predicates.payment_tendered_to_court: The tenant tendered the required money to the court.
predicates.challan_processed_before_treasury_deposi: The court processed a challan before the tenant deposited the money in the treasury under it.

issues.definition: In a rent-default eviction suit, when the tenant tenders payment to the court and a challan is processed before the later treasury deposit, the deposit dates from the tender or challan-presentation date.
